The single command of EO 11767 was the designation itself; no continuing independent command or accrued obligation is located in the held texts.

research_rationale:
EO 13762 of January 13, 2017 (82 FR 7619) set an order of succession for the office of Attorney General (section 1), exceptions (section 2), revoked EO 13557 (section 3) and added a no-rights provision (section 4). EO 13775 of February 9, 2017 (82 FR 10697) enacted a replacement succession list and in its section 3 states: "Executive Order 13762 of January 
13, 2017, is revoked." Section 1 of EO 13762 runs only until at least one named senior officer can act, a standing contingency that does not end the order. The held corpus holds no earlier revocation or amendment of EO 13762; the first and only end is February 9, 2017.
savings_reason: Section 3 of EO 13762 revoked EO 13557, and EO 13775 neither mentions EO 13557 nor restores it, so that executed revocation survives. EO 13775 reenacts a succession list in its section 1 with different officers; no acting service under EO 13762 is shown in the held texts.
earlier_end_check: Own terms: section 1 operates only during a vacancy and 'until such time as at least one of the officers mentioned above is able to perform the functions and duties of that office', a recurring contingency, not a sunset. Searched held texts by the order's number: only EO 13775 and the order's own copies cite it. No earlier revocation, supersession or amendment is held.
scope_check: Inventory is 10 scopes (a lead paragraph, sections 1 to 4 and their subsections) taken from 82 FR 7619-7620. EO 13775 section 3 revokes the whole order, so every scope ends on the same date.
independent_command_check: Section 3 of EO 13762 (revocation of EO 13557) is a one-time self-executing command and is treated in the clause reason and savings; section 4 is a no-rights statement. Neither is an independent continuing command that outlived the revocation.
savings_check: The surviving consequence is the revocation of EO 13557; EO 13775 does not reinstate it. The order of succession itself is replaced by EO 13775.

research_rationale: EO 14042 required a contract clause on COVID-19 safety protocols for federal contractors and set agency, task-force and Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council steps with dates such as October 8, 2021 and October 15, 2021; those dates are deadlines or effective dates for performance, not ends. EO 14099 of May 9, 2023, held in its Federal Register text (88 FR 30891), revoked the order in section 2 and made the revocation effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on May 12, 2023 in section 3; EO 14174 of January 21, 2025 revoked it again. The first end is May 12, 2023. The dossier's conflicts (a 2023-05-09 date from current-law, the 2025-01-21 revocation, and a whole-versus-partial reading) are resolved in the conflict resolutions.
savings_reason: Section 2 of EO 14099 provides that agency policies adopted to implement EO 14042 and premised on it no longer may be enforced and shall be rescinded consistent with applicable law, and section 4(a) only preserves agency authority granted by law. No continuing independent command or accrued right under EO 14042 is preserved in the held texts.
conflict_resolutions: {"WHOLE_END_DATE_DISAGREEMENT": "The 2023-05-09 date is the signing date of EO 14099 as read by the current-law lead; section 3 of EO 14099 makes the revocation effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on May 12, 2023, so the end is May 12, 2023. The 2025-01-21 date is EO 14174, a second revocation of an order already revoked, recorded as a later event.", "WHOLE_END_ACTOR_DISAGREEMENT": "Two orders revoke EO 14042. EO 14099 is first in time and effective earlier (May 12, 2023), so it is the actor of the first end; EO 14174 (January 21, 2025) is recorded as a later event.", "FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT": "Section 2 of EO 14099 reads, in the Federal Register text, that EO 14042 and EO 14043 are revoked, with no limitation to any part.
